title: Unbiased Teacher for Semi-Supervised Object Detection
extended_summary:
This paper addresses semi-supervised object detection, focusing on how to train object detectors when only a small labeled set and a large unlabeled set are available. The authors argue that existing pseudo-labeling approaches used in semi-supervised image classification do not transfer well to object detection because of foreground-background imbalance, foreground class imbalance, duplicated predictions, and overfitting when labeled data are scarce.

To address these issues, the paper proposes Unbiased Teacher, a teacher-student framework. A detector is first trained in a burn-in stage on labeled data. It is then duplicated into a teacher and student model: the teacher produces pseudo-labels for unlabeled images, the student learns from them, and the teacher is updated through exponential moving average (EMA) of the student. The method also uses weak augmentation for the teacher, strong augmentation for the student, class-wise NMS, confidence thresholding, and focal loss to reduce pseudo-label bias and improve stability.

The paper evaluates the method on MS-COCO and PASCAL VOC in several semi-supervised detection settings, including COCO-standard, COCO-additional, and VOC. It reports substantial gains over prior methods such as CSD and STAC, especially in low-label regimes. The main conclusion is that continuously refined teacher-student learning, together with EMA and focal loss, produces more reliable pseudo-labels and meaningfully improves semi-supervised object detection performance.

identified_tools.name: ITS (General)
identified_tools.description: A semi-supervised teacher-student object detection framework that uses pseudo-labeling, exponential moving average (EMA) teacher refinement, confidence thresholding, and focal loss to improve learning from labeled and unlabeled data.
identified_tools.use_case: Studied as a semi-supervised object detection method for training an object detector with a small labeled set and a large unlabeled set; evaluated on MS-COCO and PASCAL VOC.

findings.finding_summary: Unbiased Teacher improved object detection performance over supervised baselines and prior semi-supervised methods. On COCO-standard, it achieved 16.94 mAP at 0.5% labeled data, 20.75 mAP at 1%, 24.30 mAP at 2%, 28.27 mAP at 5%, and 31.50 mAP at 10%, compared with the supervised baselines of 6.83, 9.05, 12.70, 18.47, and 23.86 respectively.

On COCO-additional, the method outperformed supervised-only training and prior semi-supervised baselines. The reported AP50:95 was 41.30 for Ours versus 40.20 for supervised (3x), 38.82 for CSD (3x), and 39.21 for STAC (6x).

On VOC, Unbiased Teacher achieved 77.37 AP50 and 48.69 AP50:95 versus the supervised baseline of 72.63 AP50 and 42.13 AP50:95. This exceeded STAC on AP50:95 (44.64) and matched or slightly trailed it on AP50 (77.45 vs 77.37), while still showing a stronger overall detection-quality gain.
findings.measure: VOC object detection AP50 and AP50:95
findings.effect_size: +4.74 AP50 and +6.56 AP50:95 vs supervised baseline

findings.finding_summary: Ablation results showed that EMA training and focal loss improved pseudo-label balance and model performance. With COCO-standard 1% labeled data, the model using focal loss plus EMA had the best mAP (21.19) and the lowest KL-divergence between pseudo-label and ground-truth class distributions (0.0851), compared with cross-entropy without EMA (13.42 mAP; KL=1.7915).
findings.measure: Validation mAP and KL-divergence between pseudo-label and ground-truth class distributions
findings.effect_size: +7.77 mAP vs cross-entropy without EMA; KL-divergence reduced by 1.7064

quality_tier_rationale: This is an empirical conference paper with clear experimental comparisons across multiple benchmark datasets and ablation analyses. It is not a randomized educational study, but it provides a reasonably well-specified causal-style evaluation within machine learning experimentation.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported gains are large in magnitude across several settings, including double-digit mAP improvements in low-label regimes. These are substantial performance differences, though they concern computer vision detection rather than educational outcomes.
